news.headline: US-Iran Exchange of Fire Sends Crude Up 0.91%; Strait of Hormuz Risks Re-emerge
news.what_happened: The US and Iran traded strikes for the first time in approximately one month on August 31, reigniting fears over Strait of Hormuz security. WTI crude surged to $86.54/bbl and Brent to $88.84/bbl.
news.why_it_matters: Crude at $86+ is a direct cost headwind for airlines (40% of OPEX), paints (40-50% raw material), and tyres (60-70% input cost). Conversely, upstream producers ONGC and OIL India see higher per-barrel realization; OMCs get short-term inventory gains.

news.headline: FII Net Sellers of Rs 7,985.88 Cr on Aug 31; DII Bought Rs 4,588.88 Cr
news.what_happened: Foreign Institutional Investors were aggressive net sellers of Rs 7,985.88 crore in the cash market on Monday (Aug 31). DIIs countered with Rs 4,588.88 crore in buying, but could not fully offset FII pressure. Nifty 50 fell 95 points (-0.39%) to close at 24,080.
news.why_it_matters: Heavy FII outflows signal risk-off globally tied to Iran-US tensions and rising US yields at 4.758%. Continuation of FII selling today would push Nifty toward the 23,990-24,020 support zone. Mid and small caps are most exposed during FII sell periods.

news.headline: India Q1 FY27 GDP Growth Strong at 7.8%; Manufacturing Expands 9.2%
news.what_happened: India's real GDP grew 7.8% year-on-year in Q1 FY2026-27 (April-June 2026), with GVA up 8.2%, manufacturing expanding 9.2%, and investment demand accelerating to 11.9%.
news.why_it_matters: Strong domestic growth underpins earnings visibility for consumption, banking, and infrastructure sectors. Acts as a structural positive even amid short-term global risk-off. Banks with high credit growth benefit from a robust economy.

news.headline: MSCI Rebalancing Volatility from Monday Expected to Subside Today
news.what_happened: Monday's Nifty session saw sharp intraday swings in the final hour due to MSCI quarterly rebalancing flows, with several large-cap stocks seeing outsized moves unrelated to fundamentals.
news.why_it_matters: Post-rebalancing, artificial price distortions tend to reverse over 1-2 sessions. Stocks that sold off purely on MSCI-driven flows may see mean-reversion buying today, providing a technical tailwind.

picks.catalyst: WTI Crude +0.91% on US-Iran tensions; Strait of Hormuz risk premium in oil prices
picks.logic: ONGC realizes crude oil prices directly. Every $1/bbl rise in crude adds approximately Rs 1,500 Cr/year to ONGC revenues. With WTI at $86.54 and geopolitical risk premium sustained by US-Iran exchange of fire, ONGC is the cleanest upstream beneficiary on NSE. Previous close Rs 231.80.
